title: West Chester becomes Pennsylvania's newest Bird Town
summary: Bird Town Pennsylvania made the borough's designation official at a Borough Hall ceremony, crediting its pesticide-free parks and growing number of rain and pollinator gardens. Volunteers, two WCU professors and the borough's sustainability director led the push, and the borough plans bird-friendly landscaping next.

title: West Chester's F2 Strategy buys a cloud and Salesforce consultancy
summary: The West Chester wealth-management tech consulting firm has acquired Callaway Cloud Consulting, adding engineering, data and AI staff so it can build systems as well as advise on them. Callaway will take on the F2 Strategy name in early 2027.

title: West Chester biotech MTTI wins $3.17M federal grant for a lung cancer drug
summary: Molecular Targeting Technologies received a five-year National Cancer Institute grant to move its experimental radiopharmaceutical Lu-EBRGD toward clinical trials in non-small cell lung cancer.

title: Propane transfer facility cleared for Phoenixville Pike in West Goshen
summary: A 1.5-acre lot at Phoenixville Pike and Saunders Lane is set to become an above-ground propane transfer site with two 30,000-gallon tanks. West Goshen's zoning officer says the plans comply with township rules.

title: West Chester police grow beards for five local charities
summary: West Chester officers have relaxed grooming rules for three months to raise money for Unite for Her, the West Chester Food Cupboard and three other local causes. Last year's regional version of the fundraiser brought in more than $50,000.

title: Phineas Gage marks 10 years downtown with an anniversary weekend
summary: The West Chester restaurant is celebrating a decade in the borough with giveaways, discounts and celebratory drinks. Nearby Gemelli Gelato is also marking 12 years on Market Street.

title: Henderson sophomore repeats as Ches-Mont National tennis champ
summary: Erika Dunwoody beat Downingtown East's Mahi Patel 6-1, 7-5 to defend her Ches-Mont League National Division girls singles title. She moves on to the district championships next.

title: Steadicam inventor builds his Zeen mobility device in a West Chester factory
summary: Garrett Brown, who invented the Steadicam, and Exokinetics Inc. assemble the Zeen, a walker-wheelchair hybrid that lets users move between sitting and standing, at their West Chester facility. Each unit is customized, and the company says it has now built thousands.

title: Barclay Friends earns a national seal for its memory care
summary: The West Chester senior living community received the National Council of Certified Dementia Practitioners' Memory Care Excellence Network seal for 2026. Staff there complete dementia-practitioner certification plus six hours of dementia training every year.

title: County inspectors cite four West Chester-area kitchens, including WCU's Commons
summary: Sept. 28 inspections found coolers running warm and sanitation lapses at Brother's Pizza and Two Birds Cafe on Downingtown Pike and at the Freshens and Rammy's Market stations in WCU's Commons, leading to discarded food and Oct. 5 repair deadlines. A Buffalo Wild Wings To Go on West Chester Pike was cited for gaps around its exterior doors.
loc: Downingtown Pike & University Avenue, West Chester

title: Chester County's measles count climbs to 83 as officials push vaccination
summary: The state health department reports 18 new Chester County cases in the past two weeks, bringing the county's total this year to 83, third-highest in Pennsylvania. County officials urge residents to check their immunity; more than 5,300 MMR shots have been given at pop-up clinics.

title: West Bradford Fire Company launches a drive for new volunteers
summary: The all-volunteer company, which answered 417 calls in 2025 across a 32-square-mile district, has opened a recruitment website and a "Make the Choice. Be the Change." campaign. No experience is needed, training and gear are free, and roles range from apprentice firefighters age 16 and up to senior firefighters.

title: WCU plans a three-day celebration of 100 years of campus jazz
summary: West Chester University marks the centennial of its Criterions Jazz Ensemble Nov. 6-8 with a free welcome concert, a free masterclass with vibraphonist Stefon Harris, a ticketed dance soiree and a centennial concert. Proceeds support a new endowment for the jazz program.

title: West Goshen drafts licensing rules for short-term rentals
summary: Proposed rules would require short-term rental hosts to get an annual license and inspection, file floor plans and parking details, and keep a guest register, with one off-street space per bedroom and $250-a-day fines for violations. Supervisors plan to vote Oct. 20.
